en: The Amihan brings cool, dry air to the Philippines from November to February.
Volcanic ash from Mount Pinatubo enriched the soil in Central Luzon with essential minerals.
Stalactites in the Puerto Princesa Subterranean River form drop by drop from mineral-rich water.
Morning fog in Baguio City forms when warm, moist air cools and condenses.
During a total lunar eclipse, Earth's atmosphere bends sunlight to make the moon look red.
The three stars of Orion's Belt, locally called Talatuntan, point toward the bright star Sirius.
The gravitational pull of the moon causes the daily high and low tides in Manila Bay.
Heavy monsoon rains often cause rapid flash floods in low-lying areas of Metro Manila.
Dark, towering cumulonimbus clouds indicate an approaching thunderstorm with heavy rain and possible lightning.
Pumice is a light volcanic rock that floats on water because it contains many gas bubbles.
Planting deep-rooted vetiver grass along the steep slopes of Benguet prevents topsoil from washing away.
Groundwater naturally flows to the surface as a spring when it hits an impermeable rock layer.
